Subject: Kestrel pilot: proposed playbook, success metrics and GPU plan

Thanks for taking the call today — great discussion. Short recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth going into the pilot: 

1) Goals & success criteria
- Latency: 95th percentile < 180ms for 512-token responses under steady state
- Cost: median cost per 1K tokens in evaluation window to be <= agreed target (TBD in SOW)
- Quality: at least 85% pass rate on prioritized prompt set (see attached pilot-metrics-template.xlsx)
- Stability: <1% error rate during test window; no persistent out-of-memory failures

2) Pilot scope & timeline
- Kickoff/onboarding call: week of Jul 26 (proposed Tue Jul 27 10am PT)
- Warm-up: 7 days baseline traffic + synthetic load for spike testing
- Evaluation window: 28 days after warm-up for representative traffic and feature tests
- Roll decision: redact/expand based on metric gates above

3) Capacity and burst model (proposed)
- Reserved baseline: 2 x A100-class GPUs dedicated for the pilot (predictable throughput for steady test queries)
- Autoscaling policy: scale up to 6 GPUs on observed concurrency spikes or sustained 90th percentile CPU/GPU util > 70% for 3 consecutive minutes
- Burst expectations: short bursts (3-5 minutes) up to 8 GPUs allowed for load testing only; costs for burst capacity billed at overage rate in SOW
- KV / prefix cache: we will enable prefix caching for repeated sessions to reduce per-token compute during evaluation

4) Ownership & contacts
- Redwood engagement lead: Karthik (sales) — coordination, commercial items
- Solutions/infra lead: Vivek — sizing, autoscale, telemetry hooks
- Customer success: Marissa — onboarding, eval reporting, runbooks
- Customer owners: Aisha (technical PM), Tom (engineering lead)

5) Next steps (action items)
- Kestrel: confirm pilot contact list and any required compliance docs by EOD Thu Jul 22 (Aisha)
- Redwood: provide attestation + pilot metrics template (attached) and a one-page cost/burst estimate by Fri Jul 23 (Vivek)
- Schedule kickoff (Karthik to send calendar invite)

Attachments: pilot-metrics-template.xlsx (template for pass/fail prompt set); kestrel-pilot-attestation.pdf (security checklist stub)

If that aligns, I’ll send a formal one-pager + calendar invite. Happy to push the kickoff to a different day if that works better for the team.

Thanks — Karthik

+1 on Karthik’s plan. A few technical specifics to lock down before kickoff: 

- Baseline sizing rationale: 2 x A100s covers ~600 concurrent short-chat sessions (avg 150 tokens) with 95th latency target; number comes from our internal qps-per-GPU benchmark for the model size we discussed.
- Autoscale policy (recommended config to put in the prod-like cluster):
  * metric: GPU_utilization (aggregate) + queue_depth (requests waiting for scheduling)
  * scale up trigger: GPU_utilization > 70% OR queue_depth > 20 for 180s
  * scale down trigger: GPU_utilization < 45% AND queue_depth < 5 for 300s
  * cool-down window: 3 minutes for scale up, 10 minutes for scale down to avoid flapping
- Burst testing plan: we will run three controlled spike tests during warm-up to validate autoscale thresholds: 2x steady, 4x steady, and 8x steady for 3 minutes each. We will capture tail latency and error rates per test.
- KV/prefix cache sizing: allocate ~32GB of shared KV cache per node for session affinity tests; this will reduce token compute for repeated prompt prefixes by ~30% in our prior pilots.
- Telemetry hooks: enable per-request trace_id and 95/99 latency dashboards; Marissa, we should add these to the onboarding checklist so the customer can verify during the warm-up window.

Cost note — high level (will be refined in formal estimate): baseline reserved 2 GPUs = X/day; burst overage for short spikes billed by GPU-minute after reserved baseline exhausted. I’ll send the draft numbers separately (Vivek).

-Vivek
